1-1-division-and-differentiation-in-huma.label: Question 1
1-1-division-and-differentiation-in-huma.exp: Body tissues are made of somatic cells, which divide by mitosis to make more identical diploid cells.

1-1-division-and-differentiation-in-huma.label: Question 1
1-1-division-and-differentiation-in-huma.exp: Embryonic stem cells are undifferentiated and pluripotent, so they can form almost all cell types.

1-1-division-and-differentiation-in-huma.label: Question 2
1-1-division-and-differentiation-in-huma.exp: New cases rise by about 2000 between 55–59 and 60–64, the biggest rise. Frequency peaks at 85+, falls at 80–84, and is about 300 when cases are 4800.

1-1-division-and-differentiation-in-huma.label: Question 1
1-1-division-and-differentiation-in-huma.exp: All body cells contain the same genes, but differentiation switches different genes on, so each cell type makes different proteins.

1-1-division-and-differentiation-in-huma.label: Question 2
1-1-division-and-differentiation-in-huma.exp: Diploid germline cells divide by mitosis to make more germline cells, and by meiosis to make haploid gametes.

1-1-division-and-differentiation-in-huma.label: Question 3
1-1-division-and-differentiation-in-huma.exp: Blood is a connective tissue. 4 of its 20 cells are dividing: 4 ÷ 20 × 100 = 20%.

1-1-division-and-differentiation-in-huma.label: Question 1
1-1-division-and-differentiation-in-huma.exp: Germline cells divide by meiosis to produce haploid gametes.

1-1-division-and-differentiation-in-huma.label: Question 1
1-1-division-and-differentiation-in-huma.exp: Corneal repair and skin regeneration use stem cells to treat patients (therapeutic). Drug testing is a research use.

1-1-division-and-differentiation-in-huma.label: Question 2
1-1-division-and-differentiation-in-huma.exp: Rectal cancer costs £4000 early and £12 000 late. The £8000 saving is 8000 ÷ 12 000 = 67% less.

1-1-division-and-differentiation-in-huma.label: Question 1
1-1-division-and-differentiation-in-huma.exp: Germline cells divide by meiosis, which halves the chromosome number to give haploid gametes.

1-1-division-and-differentiation-in-huma.label: Question 1
1-1-division-and-differentiation-in-huma.exp: Red blood cells come from multipotent tissue (adult) stem cells in the bone marrow.

1-1-division-and-differentiation-in-huma.label: Question 3
1-1-division-and-differentiation-in-huma.exp: For 50–59, survival is 96% and new cases are 10%. 96 : 10 simplifies to 48 : 5.

1-2-structure-and-replication-of-dna.label: Question 3
1-2-structure-and-replication-of-dna.exp: The sample is heated (3) so the strands separate (4), then cooled so primers bind (1), and finally heat-tolerant DNA polymerase replicates the DNA (2).

1-2-structure-and-replication-of-dna.label: Question 4
1-2-structure-and-replication-of-dna.exp: Each nucleotide has one deoxyribose. 144 base pairs is 288 nucleotides, so 288 sugars.

1-2-structure-and-replication-of-dna.label: Question 1
1-2-structure-and-replication-of-dna.exp: 1200 cytosine means 1200 guanine, so 2400 C + G. That leaves 5600 A + T, and A = T, so 2800 adenine.

1-2-structure-and-replication-of-dna.label: Question 3
1-2-structure-and-replication-of-dna.exp: A : C is 1 : 3, so A is 1/8 and C is 3/8 of the bases (A = T, C = G). G = 3/8 × 12 000 = 4500.

1-2-structure-and-replication-of-dna.label: Question 4
1-2-structure-and-replication-of-dna.exp: The strands are antiparallel. A strand's 5' end finishes with a phosphate and its 3' end with deoxyribose; only C labels both strands this way.

1-2-structure-and-replication-of-dna.label: Question 2
1-2-structure-and-replication-of-dna.exp: The lagging strand is built in fragments, and these fragments are joined by ligase.

1-2-structure-and-replication-of-dna.label: Question 3
1-2-structure-and-replication-of-dna.exp: 4 more cycles doubles 32 four times to 512 copies. 512 − 32 = 480 additional copies.

1-2-structure-and-replication-of-dna.label: Question 2
1-2-structure-and-replication-of-dna.exp: Adenine = thymine = 1245. T : G is 3 : 2, so G = 1245 ÷ 3 × 2 = 830.

1-2-structure-and-replication-of-dna.label: Question 10
1-2-structure-and-replication-of-dna.exp: Starting from one copy, 256 copies needs 8 cycles (2⁸ = 256). 8 × 3 temperature changes = 24.

1-2-structure-and-replication-of-dna.label: Question 1
1-2-structure-and-replication-of-dna.exp: DNA contains the sugar deoxyribose, and complementary bases are held together by hydrogen bonds.

1-2-structure-and-replication-of-dna.label: Question 2
1-2-structure-and-replication-of-dna.exp: DNA polymerase adds DNA nucleotides to the 3' end of a growing strand.

1-2-structure-and-replication-of-dna.label: Question 6
1-2-structure-and-replication-of-dna.exp: 128 copies needs 7 cycles. Each cycle has 3 temperature stages of 2 minutes: 7 × 6 = 42 minutes.

1-2-structure-and-replication-of-dna.label: Question 2
1-2-structure-and-replication-of-dna.exp: 20 minutes is 10 cycles, and each cycle doubles the DNA: 2¹⁰ = 1024.

1-3-gene-expression.label: Question 2
1-3-gene-expression.exp: The primary transcript is the RNA copy of the whole gene, so it still contains introns and exons. Introns are removed by splicing to give mature mRNA.

1-3-gene-expression.label: Question 3
1-3-gene-expression.exp: The codons are AUG CCA ACU CCU AGA CGA AUA: Met, Pro, Thr, Pro, Arg, Arg, Ile. Pro and Arg repeat, leaving 5 different amino acids.

1-3-gene-expression.label: Question 6
1-3-gene-expression.exp: RNA splicing removes the introns from the primary transcript, joining the exons to make mature mRNA.

1-3-gene-expression.label: Question 2
1-3-gene-expression.exp: The mRNA codon is complementary to DNA GAT, with U instead of T: CUA. The tRNA anticodon is complementary to the codon: GAU.

1-3-gene-expression.label: Question 3
1-3-gene-expression.exp: The 24 bases make 8 codons. AUG and GCU each appear twice, leaving 6 different codons, so 6 different amino acids are coded for.

1-3-gene-expression.label: Question 4
1-3-gene-expression.exp: Transcription (X) happens in the nucleus, then RNA splicing (Y) makes mature mRNA, and translation (Z) happens at the ribosome.

1-3-gene-expression.label: Question 4
1-3-gene-expression.exp: Translation needs mRNA (the code), tRNA (carries amino acids) and rRNA (part of the ribosome), but not DNA.

1-3-gene-expression.label: Question 4
1-3-gene-expression.exp: mRNA travels to ribosomes in the cytoplasm, tRNA carries amino acids there, and rRNA forms part of the ribosomes.

1-3-gene-expression.label: Question 5
1-3-gene-expression.exp: Transcription uses DNA as a template to make mRNA. tRNA and rRNA are used in translation.

1-3-gene-expression.label: Question 1
1-3-gene-expression.exp: X (block 2) ends up in a mature mRNA, so it is an exon. Different exons kept from the same primary mRNA is alternative splicing.

1-4-mutations.label: Question 4
1-4-mutations.exp: Missense swaps one amino acid for another (2), nonsense gives an early stop codon (3), and splice-site mutations alter exon-intron boundaries (1).

1-4-mutations.label: Question 2
1-4-mutations.exp: An inserted nucleotide shifts the reading frame, so every codon after it is changed: a frame-shift mutation.

1-4-mutations.label: Question 5
1-4-mutations.exp: In B, UAC (tyrosine) changes to UAG, which is a stop codon, so translation ends early and the protein is shortened.

1-4-mutations.label: Question 5
1-4-mutations.exp: One base (G) has been swapped for another (T) with no change in length: a substitution.

1-4-mutations.label: Question 2
1-4-mutations.exp: Single gene mutations alter nucleotides by deletion, substitution or insertion.

1-4-mutations.label: Question 5
1-4-mutations.exp: P has genes 9 and 10 repeated (duplication), Q has 7–10 reversed (inversion), and R has new genes 15 and 16 from another chromosome (translocation).

1-4-mutations.label: Question 7
1-4-mutations.exp: A nonsense mutation changes a codon into a premature stop codon, so a shorter protein is made.

1-4-mutations.label: Question 8
1-4-mutations.exp: One chromosome in the middle pair has lost a section (deletion), and a section of another chromosome has joined a non-homologous one (translocation).

1-4-mutations.label: Question 3
1-4-mutations.exp: A section added from a non-homologous chromosome is translocation (3), a reversed section is inversion (1), and a section from the homologous partner is duplication (2).

1-5-human-genomics.label: Question 5
1-5-human-genomics.exp: Each cut adds one fragment. Enzyme 1 cuts twice (3 fragments), enzyme 2 cuts three times (4 fragments), and both together make 5 cuts (6 fragments).

1-5-human-genomics.label: Question 7
1-5-human-genomics.exp: DNA probes are short single strands that bind to a matching sequence, so they detect that sequence in a sample.

1-5-human-genomics.label: Question 6
1-5-human-genomics.exp: Enzyme X cuts once at 12 kb, so it gives fragments of 12 kb and 40 − 12 = 28 kb.

1-5-human-genomics.label: Question 7
1-5-human-genomics.exp: Pharmacogenetics is using a person's genome to choose effective drugs and doses.

1-5-human-genomics.label: Question 3
1-5-human-genomics.exp: The harmful mRNA is ACUU, so the DNA template has TGAA. Only C, GCTGAAT, contains TGAA.

1-5-human-genomics.label: Question 5
1-5-human-genomics.exp: Pharmacogenetics uses genome information to choose the right drugs and doses.

1-5-human-genomics.label: Question 7
1-5-human-genomics.exp: Pharmacogenetics uses a patient's gene sequences to choose the right drug and dose.

1-7-cellular-respiration.label: Question 7
1-7-cellular-respiration.exp: Glucose breakdown is the dashed line, read on the right-hand axis. At 1% oxygen it is 2·5 units per minute.

1-7-cellular-respiration.label: Question 5
1-7-cellular-respiration.exp: Dehydrogenases remove hydrogen ions and electrons from substrates and pass them to NAD, forming NADH.

1-7-cellular-respiration.label: Question 6
1-7-cellular-respiration.exp: 40 mm ÷ 10 000 = 0·004 mm. Multiply by 1000 to give 4 micrometres.

1-7-cellular-respiration.label: Question 7
1-7-cellular-respiration.exp: X shows the high-energy electrons from NADH being passed along the carrier proteins of the electron transport chain.

1-7-cellular-respiration.label: Question 8
1-7-cellular-respiration.exp: High levels of ATP and citrate show the cell has enough energy, so they inhibit phosphofructokinase and slow glycolysis.

1-7-cellular-respiration.label: Question 9
1-7-cellular-respiration.exp: After two weeks, about 0·6 kg protein, 4 kg fat and 1·5 kg carbohydrate have been lost: about 6 kg in total. 60 − 6 = 54 kg.

1-7-cellular-respiration.label: Question 5
1-7-cellular-respiration.exp: Glycolysis happens in the cytoplasm and needs no mitochondria. The other processes need a nucleus or mitochondria.

1-7-cellular-respiration.label: Question 6
1-7-cellular-respiration.exp: Hydrogen ions flowing back through ATP synthase drive the synthesis of most of the cell's ATP.

1-7-cellular-respiration.label: Question 7
1-7-cellular-respiration.exp: Glycolysis makes ATP from ADP + Pi and forms NADH. Converting pyruvate to lactate uses that NADH and regenerates NAD.

1-7-cellular-respiration.label: Question 8
1-7-cellular-respiration.exp: Glycolysis makes ATP (4) and pyruvate (2), pyruvate becomes an acetyl group (1), and acetyl combines with oxaloacetate to form citrate (3).

1-7-cellular-respiration.label: Question 9
1-7-cellular-respiration.exp: ATP synthase makes ATP, and oxygen accepts the electrons and hydrogen ions to form water.

1-7-cellular-respiration.label: Question 10
1-7-cellular-respiration.exp: Oxygen is the final electron acceptor, combining with hydrogen ions and electrons to form water.

1-7-cellular-respiration.label: Question 5
1-7-cellular-respiration.exp: Oxygen is only used at the end of the electron transport chain, as the final electron acceptor.

1-7-cellular-respiration.label: Question 6
1-7-cellular-respiration.exp: An acetyl group (X) joins coenzyme A to form acetyl coenzyme A, which combines with oxaloacetate (Y) to form citrate (Z).

1-7-cellular-respiration.label: Question 9
1-7-cellular-respiration.exp: Oxaloacetate combines with acetyl coenzyme A to form citrate, and is regenerated in the citric acid cycle.

1-7-cellular-respiration.label: Question 9
1-7-cellular-respiration.exp: ATP falls from 38 to 2, a drop of 36. 36 ÷ 38 × 100 = 95%.

1-7-cellular-respiration.label: Question 10
1-7-cellular-respiration.exp: D is ATP synthase, the membrane protein that hydrogen ions flow back through to make ATP.

1-7-cellular-respiration.label: Question 4
1-7-cellular-respiration.exp: Glass beads take up the same volume as the organism but do not respire, so any change shows the organism caused it.

1-7-cellular-respiration.label: Question 9
1-7-cellular-respiration.exp: Without enough oxygen, pyruvate is converted to lactate, which regenerates NAD so glycolysis can keep going.

1-8-energy-systems-in-muscle-cells.label: Question 11
1-8-energy-systems-in-muscle-cells.exp: 100 m athletes have 80% fast twitch fibres; 800 m athletes have 40%. That is twice as many.

1-8-energy-systems-in-muscle-cells.label: Question 11
1-8-energy-systems-in-muscle-cells.exp: Slow-twitch fibres generate ATP by aerobic respiration and contain many mitochondria.

1-8-energy-systems-in-muscle-cells.label: Question 12
1-8-energy-systems-in-muscle-cells.exp: Regular training improved the time by 50 s (830 to 780); HIIT improved it by 80 s (820 to 740). 80 − 50 = 30 s.

1-8-energy-systems-in-muscle-cells.label: Question 7
1-8-energy-systems-in-muscle-cells.exp: Heart rate rose from 60 to 120 bpm in 5 minutes: 60 ÷ 5 = 12 bpm per minute.

1-8-energy-systems-in-muscle-cells.label: Question 8
1-8-energy-systems-in-muscle-cells.exp: Sprinters rely on fast-twitch fibres, which have relatively few mitochondria.

1-8-energy-systems-in-muscle-cells.label: Question 10
1-8-energy-systems-in-muscle-cells.exp: Females took 40 min alone and 30 min in a race. The 10 min improvement is 10 ÷ 40 = 25%.

1-8-energy-systems-in-muscle-cells.label: Question 11
1-8-energy-systems-in-muscle-cells.exp: A long ski race needs endurance: slow-twitch fibres with many mitochondria, a large blood supply and aerobic respiration.

1-8-energy-systems-in-muscle-cells.label: Question 9
1-8-energy-systems-in-muscle-cells.exp: When the oxygen debt is repaid, lactate is converted back to pyruvate and glucose in the liver.

1-8-energy-systems-in-muscle-cells.label: Question 10
1-8-energy-systems-in-muscle-cells.exp: In one minute (60 000 ms) the fast fibre contracts 60 000 ÷ 75 = 800 times and the slow fibre 60 000 ÷ 100 = 600 times. 800 − 600 = 200.

1-8-energy-systems-in-muscle-cells.label: Question 11
1-8-energy-systems-in-muscle-cells.exp: Sprinters have more fast-twitch fibres: lower myoglobin, higher glycogen and fewer mitochondria.
